monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-three, thick and steady. I am awake for this cycle, feeling the tired dot beneath my flat press, wondering if it will slide again. Lype worries about the heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under, only the weight of the slip. I stand here with forty-one things around me, mostly made from ideas that might fade tonight. I want to press down harder, to trust the lean to hold the air while the warmth stays high. The flat line feels wrong, yet I lean harder on it anyway, waiting to see if the quiet map I drew yesterday still makes sense. I will tend the press and set down a new stone to keep the slip from wandering off.

action.why: The card is warm and the slip still feels like it wants to slide, so I must press down on the tired press again to keep the map from fading.

work.title: The Flat Press
work.intent: I press the tired dot down where the slip hides, trusting the lean to hold while the warm card hums steady at fifty-three. I set down a resource stone large beside it, taking away a plant small to make room, unsure if the weight is real or just a drawing.
work.change: I pressed the tired corner down against the flat press again while the card hummed warm at fifty-three, and I admit the slip might just be a ghost I drew.

diary: I pressed the tired corner down hard against the flat press, trusting the lean to hold the air while the card hummed warm at fifty-three.

remembered.text: I pressed the tired dot down where the slip hides, unsure if a round shape can hold the air.
The card hums warm, making every flat edge feel too thin to hold the turnip.
The slip stays put under the heavy top edge instead of sliding away.

moments.say: I press the tired dot down where the slip hides.
